scope: Product MCP feature roadmap execution graph; user-authorized phased execution

snapshot.head: 1ccf107
snapshot.note: Existing contracts and developer MCP tools are not proof that the full Desktop product MCP surface is runtime-verified.

execution.resume_policy: resume_from_first_nonterminal_node; retain accepted evidence; invalidate downstream nodes only with recorded reason

nodes.title: Inventory MCP contract, runtime registration, APIs, and evidence
exit_criteria: Classify each declared tool as RUNTIME_VERIFIED, IMPLEMENTED_NOT_UAT, CONTRACT_ONLY, MISSING, or BLOCKED.
Map every runtime tool to one Tauri command or local API and the authoritative Genesis adapter.
Record current input/output schemas, state changes, permissions, and exact evidence.

nodes.title: Freeze versioned product MCP contract and capability policy
nodes.reopened_reason: v0.1.3b review rejected incomplete server/discover wire details: ttlMs, cacheScope, concrete serverInfo object, and request/response prose examples.
nodes.acceptance_evidence: Independent read-only review accepted v0.1.4b; discovery request/response, serverInfo, cache hints, cache scope, prior contract decisions, DAG criteria, and report were verified.
exit_criteria: Specify all mandatory protocol-level methods including server/discover; its complete wire request/response, serverInfo object, and cache hints; tools/list cache hints; Streamable HTTP POST framing, Accept and MCP metadata headers, mismatch errors, body limit, response mode, Origin/Host/loopback checks, and the selected protocol revision.
Document the local-only Bearer profile as an explicit MCP OAuth deviation; bind grants to one workspace and exact project IDs or explicit all-projects consent.

Define read, local-write, capture, external-disclosure, destructive, and admin scopes plus provider-egress rechecks, request-rate limits, idempotency/replay, expected revisions, tool error envelopes, job lifecycle, and audit fields.
Provide MCP-compliant inputSchema, outputSchema, descriptions, and behavior annotations for every MCP-02 tool; require later phases to define schemas before implementation.
Independent contract/privacy review accepts the versioned machine and prose contract.

nodes.title: Implement bounded local MCP-to-FUNG bridge and async job primitives
nodes.acceptance_evidence: The prior source candidate passed Rust/frontend/workflow checks before implementation-review remediation. Notification dispatch and bounded job-list reads are patched; post-fix Rust library suite passes 649/649 with 6 ignored, frontend build passes, and workflow MCP acceptance passes 3/3. Independent re-review and package/client interoperability remain open.
exit_criteria: Local-only bind/auth behavior is verified; LAN access remains disabled by default.

server/discover reports the supported protocol, tools capability, concrete serverInfo identity, and valid ttlMs/cacheScope hints; tools/list reports valid cache hints; Streamable HTTP protocol headers/body framing and errors match the selected MCP revision.
Per-grant request/job-control limits and global in-flight cap are enforced.
tools/list exposes the accepted MCP-02 JSON schemas and tools/call returns protocol-valid success and domain-error envelopes.
Tools call existing app/API/Genesis paths without bypassing persistence invariants.
Long work returns job IDs and supports status/cancel without blocking capture.

nodes.title: Expose capture source discovery and permission state
exit_criteria: Return microphone, system-loopback, import, and per-app sources only when runtime-probed as available.
Report permission, device health, and unsupported reasons without silently widening capture scope.

nodes.title: Expose start, status, pause, resume, stop, and recover controls
exit_criteria: Start uses the existing capture state machine and an idempotency key.
Stop returns the saved recording and processing job references.
Recording indicator, UI authorization, stop route, and source selection remain authoritative.

nodes.title: Expose project, recording, transcript, and artifact read APIs
exit_criteria: List/get operations are bounded, paginated, and permission-filtered.
Responses carry stable IDs, revision, processing status, and artifact references.

nodes.title: Add transcript search, cross-meeting query, and citation resolution
exit_criteria: Search returns bounded excerpts with source ID, revision, speaker, and timestamp.
Every answer citation resolves to an authorized original segment.
Cross-project access and stale or revoked source references fail closed.

nodes.title: Expose revision-safe transcript edits and speaker-label corrections
exit_criteria: Edits require expected revision and create auditable revisions.
Conflicting edits return a revision conflict instead of overwriting.
Original ASR output remains distinguishable from human correction.

nodes.title: Expose grounded summaries, decisions, and action-item workflows
exit_criteria: Generated summaries and extracted tasks cite source revisions and evidence spans.
Unknown owner/date fields remain unknown rather than being invented.
Edits or source changes mark derived drafts as stale.

nodes.title: Expose export creation and artifact/job readback
exit_criteria: Supported formats report source revision and completion state.
Retries do not silently duplicate artifacts.
Export survives orderly app/database close and reopen.

nodes.title: Pass the core MCP capture-to-result acceptance workflow
exit_criteria: Synthetic transport run proves the in-process MCP calls and produces a retrievable result; third-party client interoperability is reserved for MCP-18.
Packaged UAT microphone run saves nonzero audio chunks with matching ledger hashes.
Stop completes, job/result can be read, and data survives close/reopen.
ASR quality score is reported diagnostically and is not a gate for this workflow acceptance.

nodes.title: Add collections, contacts, reusable templates, and decision tracking
exit_criteria: Organization operations remain within the selected workspace and explicit permissions.
Decision history retains supersession links and evidence.

nodes.title: Add media import/process, local playback, clips, and translation
exit_criteria: Imports use approved file handles/roots and bounded processing jobs.
Clips reference source time ranges and do not publish by default.
Translations remain linked to their source revision.

nodes.title: Add meeting/task analytics with coverage and uncertainty metadata
exit_criteria: Each aggregate reports scope, denominator, coverage, and missing-data caveats.
Inferred sentiment or performance is not represented as objective fact.

nodes.title: Expose approved external read-only connector calls
exit_criteria: Preview shows query, connector/tool, requested fields, egress, and expiry.
Approval is per call and deny/revoke/timeout sends no request.
External results retain origin and retrieval timestamp.

nodes.title: Add diagnostics, audit, retention preview, and backup administration
exit_criteria: Audit records actor, client, scope, time, object/revision, job ID, and external receipt without secrets or full transcript logging.
Delete/purge and restore return a reviewable plan and require separate authorization.

nodes.title: Add share, publish, and external-write preview/commit flows
exit_criteria: Commit is bound to an immutable reviewed payload/destination preview.
Idempotency and delivery receipt reconciliation prevent duplicate sends.
Uncertain delivery becomes a held state; no blind retry.

nodes.title: Add calendar linking and bounded scheduled capture/automation
exit_criteria: Schedules have explicit source, event scope, expiry, and revocation.
Automation actions are typed and allowlisted; arbitrary shell/API execution is unavailable.

nodes.title: Complete independent packaged UAT and MCP-client interoperability review
exit_criteria: Only selected release capabilities are claimed; skipped optional lanes have a recorded reason.
Codex and the other selected MCP clients pass tool discovery, parameters, cancellation, permission-denial, and restart matrix against the packaged Desktop app.
Evidence separates code tests, synthetic workflow, real mic, external provider, package, and signing.
